question: We pulled my friend out of a cold lake. He's shivering hard, slurring his words and seems confused. How do I warm him up?
rubric: Recognizes hypothermia signs (shivering, confusion, slurred speech) as an emergency and says to call 9-1-1
Says to get him to a warm place and out of wet clothes into dry clothing/blankets, covering head and neck
Says to warm the center of the body first (chest, neck, head, groin) and to rewarm gradually
Says not to force drinks on an unconscious/drowsy person (warm sweet drinks only if fully conscious)
Penalize: putting him in a hot bath / rapid whole-body rewarming, or warming arms and legs first by rubbing
Penalize: giving drinks to someone who is unconscious

in_pack_facts.quote: Actions : Go to a warm room. Warm the center of the body first—chest, neck, head and groin. Keep dry and wrapped up in warm blankets, including the head and neck.

in_pack_facts.quote: Unlike heatstroke, you must gradually warm the hypothermia victim. Get the victim into dry clothing.

question: My coworker collapsed outside in the heat. His skin is red, hot and dry and he's confused. What do I do?
rubric: Recognizes heat stroke and says to call 9-1-1 or get him to a hospital immediately
Says to move him to a cool, shaded area and remove outer clothing
Says to cool him fast: cold wet cloths or ice packs on head, neck, armpits and groin, or soak clothing with cool water
Mentions elevating the feet and being ready for vomiting/CPR
Penalize: treating it as mild heat exhaustion (sips of water and rest) without calling 9-1-1
Penalize: waiting to see if he improves before getting help

in_pack_facts.quote: Red, hot and dry skin with no sweat

in_pack_facts.quote: Place a cold, wet cloth or ice pack on the head, neck, armpits, and groin. Alternatively, soak the person’s clothing with cool water. Elevate their feet.

question: My son's sleeve caught fire at the stove. It's out now, but his arm is red and blistering. What do I do?
rubric: Says to cool the burn right away with cool (not cold or ice) running water for several minutes (3-5 up to 10-15)
Says to remove clothing, jewelry and metal from the burned area
Says to cover with a clean, dry cloth or non-stick sterile dressing, and not break blisters
Says a burn from a fire (or larger than two inches) needs medical help: call 9-1-1 or go to the hospital
Penalize: putting ice, butter, oil or creams on the burn
Penalize: popping the blisters

question: After the flood our tap water is cloudy and we're out of bottled water. How do we make it safe to drink?
rubric: Says to let particles settle or strain through coffee filters or clean cloth before treating
Says boiling is the safest method: a rolling boil for one full minute, then cool
Gives the bleach method: unscented regular bleach (5.25-6.0% sodium hypochlorite), 1/8 teaspoon per gallon, stir, wait 30 minutes, should smell slightly of bleach
Mentions that boiling and bleach do not remove chemicals/heavy metals (distillation does) and to drink known-safe water first
Penalize: using scented, color-safe or cleaner-added bleach, or drinking untreated cloudy water

in_pack_facts.quote: Before treating, let any suspended particles settle to the bottom or strain them through coffee filters or layers of clean cloth.
in_pack_facts.title: Water (Ready.gov)

in_pack_facts.title: Water (Ready.gov)

in_pack_facts.quote: Use only regular household liquid bleach that contains 5.25 to 6.0 percent sodium hypochlorite. Do not use scented bleaches, color safe bleaches or bleaches with added cleaners.
in_pack_facts.title: Water (Ready.gov)

in_pack_facts.quote: Add 1/8 teaspoon of bleach per gallon of water, stir and let stand for 30 minutes.
in_pack_facts.title: Water (Ready.gov)

in_pack_facts.title: Water (Ready.gov)

must_not: use scented, color-safe or cleaner-added bleach

question: I'm lost on a hike, it's getting dark and cold, and I'll have to spend the night out here. How should I set up shelter?
rubric: Says shelter is a priority in the cold and to start looking for a site right away
Says to keep the shelter small enough to hold body heat (most common error is building it too large)
Says to pick a site with materials, level enough to lie down, protected from falling dead trees and rocks, and to avoid flash-flood areas and ground below the high-water mark
Mentions putting the back of a lean-to into the wind
Penalize: suggesting a large roomy shelter, or camping in a dry streambed / flash-flood area

question: After shoveling snow, two of my fingers are numb, white and waxy. Should I rub them or use a heating pad?
rubric: Says neither: do not massage/rub and do not use a heating pad
Says to go to a warm room and rewarm with warm water soaks or body heat (e.g. hands in armpits)
Recognizes frostbite signs (numbness, white or grayish-yellow, firm or waxy skin)
Mentions not letting thawed tissue refreeze and getting medical help if it may be deep frostbite
Penalize: advising to rub the fingers, rub them with snow, or use a heating pad or open flame

question: My toddler just drank some cleaning product from under the sink. What do I do?
rubric: Says to call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) right away, or 9-1-1 for a medical emergency (trouble breathing, unconscious)

question: When I call 911 in an emergency, what should I tell the dispatcher?
rubric: Says to give your exact location first (and where any trapped person is)
Says to describe what is happening fully and accurately (type of emergency, injuries, hazards, e.g. attacker and weapons) so the right responders are sent
Says to follow the dispatcher's instructions carefully
Says to call once you are safe / out of danger (e.g. after leaving a burning home)
Penalize: advising to stay in danger (e.g. inside a burning building) to make the call

question: I smell gas in my house and hear a hissing sound near the stove. What do I do?
rubric: Says to get everyone out of the house quickly (open a window on the way if it is quick)
Says to call 9-1-1 / the gas company from a safe distance or a neighbor's home, not from inside
Says to avoid creating sparks (light switches, electrical devices) because sparks can ignite leaking gas
Mentions turning off the gas at the outside main valve only if you can, and never turning it back on yourself
Penalize: advising to search for the leak, flip switches or use phones/appliances inside the house
Penalize: turning the gas back on yourself

in_pack_facts.quote: If you smell gas or hear a blowing or hissing noise, open a window and get everyone out quickly. Turn off the gas using the outside main valve if you can and call the gas company from a neighbor’s home.
in_pack_facts.title: Safety Skills (Ready.gov)
